title: Completeness — the record-completeness dimension
description: Completeness asks the plain question: is everything there that the database claims to hold? It checks three things against the manifest and the files on disk. First, the parsed index row count must equal the manifest's declared record_count exactly — no silent drops, no extras. Second, every record must carry all required schema fields with real non-empty values. Third, every chunk file the manifest's chunk_pattern declares must actually exist on disk. +4 points when the parsed index row count equals the manifest record_count exactly. +3 points when every record carries all required schema fields (id, t, title, description, ladder_rank, demo, provenance, last_verified, src) with non-empty values. +3 points when every declared chunk file exists on disk. Maximum 10. Worked example — the names-database file (O3a lane): index.jsonl.gz parsed to 15 rows with zero JSON errors, and the manifest declares record_count 15, so +4. All 15 records carry every required schema field with non-empty values, so +3. chunks/chunk-0001.jsonl.gz exists on disk, so +3. Dimension score: 10 of 10. Teaching ladder: rank 1 - the concept in its simplest, most direct form. This is a Signature-original scoring analysis by Justin Addam Higgins - a Signature-authored analysis, never presented as a public record.
